text:
jamal: customer reports svc.payments.internal.acme resolving to NXDOMAIN from their app in prod behind the bastion. started after last-night bastion image update. API calls fail intermittently with TLS handshake timeouts + NXDOMAIN. ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFR-1234 :warning:

maria: can you paste a quick `dig` from the bastion and from an app host? also include traceroute if available.

jamal: on bastion:
```
$ dig +short svc.payments.internal.acme @10.0.0.10

;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 4321
```
from app pod (node-local):
```
$ dig +short svc.payments.internal.acme @127.0.0.53

;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 8765
```

ops-bot: bastion-egress-policy changed 2026-03-15T22:10:12Z by infra: allowed_outbound: [TCP:443, TCP:22, UDP:53] denied: [TCP:53 to 0.0.0.0/0]. Forwarder IPs in VPC: 10.0.0.10, 10.0.0.11.

samir: likely hit by DNS forwarding chain. Typical path is: nodelocal -> VPC resolver (10.0.0.10) -> Route53 private hosted zone (split-horizon). If the bastion can't reach the VPC forwarder over TCP/53 for larger responses or for fallback, queries can return NXDOMAIN under some resolver configs.

support-eng: reproduce checklist:
- run `dig +trace svc.payments.internal.acme` on bastion
- run `sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 port 53` while issuing a query
- check `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id ZXXXXXXXX` and `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints` for assoc

jamal: tcpdump while reproducing shows:
```
12:34:56.789012 IP 10.0.0.5.51515 > 10.0.0.10.53: UDP, length 72
12:34:56.789345 IP 10.0.0.10.53 > 10.0.0.5.51515: UDP, length 92
12:34:56.789400 IP 10.0.0.5.51515 > 10.0.0.10.53: TCP, Flags [S], seq 0
12:34:56.789800 IP 10.0.0.10.53 > 10.0.0.5.51515: TCP, RST
```
Shows TCP connections to 10.0.0.10 being reset — matches ops-bot policy blocking TCP/53 to 0.0.0.0/0 (bastion policy was tightened).

maria: workaround (short-term): add /etc/hosts entry on bastion for svc.payments.internal.acme -> internal ip of service (from Route53 records) so deployments can proceed. Not great for scale but quick.

samir: long-term fix options:
- allow TCP/53 from bastion -> VPC resolver IPs (10.0.0.10/11) in egress allowlist (preferred)
- confirm Route53 private hosted zone remains associated with customer VPCs and resolver rules priority is correct (rules should forward for `internal.acme` to Route53)
- ensure node-local cache isn't configured to short-circuit when forwarder unreachable (check nodelocal config `upstream` list)

support-eng: exact infra change request text to escalate:
"Please update bastion egress allowlist to permit TCP/53 and UDP/53 to the VPC resolver forwarder IPs 10.0.0.10 and 10.0.0.11. This is required so DNS queries for private Route53 hosted zones (split-horizon) can complete; current TCP resets cause NXDOMAINs for service endpoints (svc.payments.internal.acme). Request impact: restores prod app DNS resolution and prevents TLS handshake failures. Ticket: INFR-1234. ETA needed: asap / within 2 hours."

jamal: I've filed the infra escalation and attached tcpdump + dig outputs to the ticket. tagging infra: @maria @samir please follow up with change and confirm when TCP/53 is allowed to the forwarders.

maria: acked. will ping infra rotations and follow up on the change window. once allowed, re-run the `dig` and tcpdump.

support-eng: post-change verification steps (to run after infra confirms rule change):
1) `dig +short svc.payments.internal.acme @10.0.0.10` should return the internal IP (not empty).
2) `dig +trace svc.payments.internal.acme` should show forwarding to 10.0.0.10 and answer from Route53.
3) run a quick canary deployment to the app to ensure TLS handshakes succeed and no 5xx spikes.

samir: note for follow-up: consider adding a resolver healthcheck alert (forwarder connection failures) to catch this earlier next time.

jamal: thanks all — will update the customer once infra confirms. :thumbsup:
